title: Catalyst rods: c11's ringed active-nematic droplets made to grow only through identity-carrying catalyst particles on a fed fuel settle from noise into a turning-over population of ~16 ringed, swimming rods that split and vanish
summary: c11's ringed active-nematic world with its supersaturated bath replaced by an undersaturated one (phi_b -0.8, so droplets shrink by themselves) and droplet material made only by Brownian catalyst particles from a fed, diffusing fuel (prod = kc Ky c u); the particles replicate inside droplets, die faster outside, ride the self-made flow and are gated by droplet material, and carry a heritable rate y and an inert marker (mutation off here). From noise about 30 droplets nucleate, grow into rods and then settle by t~500 at 15-17 rods (occupancy 0.06) that keep splitting (90 splits, 11 persistent, generation 2), merging (29) and disappearing, with a surfactant layer at their edge (labkit rim/core 1.55, rim/out 2.32, 87/122 membrane-like) and motion up to 3.5 body lengths (pack/seed0/sheet.png, timeseries.png). Without particle death in the bath or at higher fuel it becomes a dense churning emulsion, and at lower fuel it dies out (data/screens.txt).
